title: Finite-probability protocols bound private-coin complexity
statement: Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be the function to be computed, and let $\Omega_X$ and $\Omega_Y$ be finite probability spaces serving as the two players' private randomness. Fix real numbers $\varepsilon'$ and $\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon' < \varepsilon$, and let $p$ be a finite-message private-coin protocol with randomness spaces $\Omega_X$ and $\Omega_Y$, input types $X$ and $Y$, and output type $\alpha$, and suppose that $p$ computes $f$ with error at most $\varepsilon'$, i.e.\ for every input pair $(x,y)$ the probability that $p$ returns a value other than $f(x,y)$ is at most $\varepsilon'$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error private-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$ satisfies $R_\varepsilon(f) \le \mathrm{complexity}(p)$, where the right-hand side is the worst-case number of bits exchanged by $p$.
hypotheses_covered: Ω_X, Ω_Y are finite probability spaces
f : X → Y → α is the target function
p is a finite-message private-coin protocol over Ω_X, Ω_Y
p ε'-approximately computes f (error ≤ ε' on every input)

This is the key reduction step showing that protocols over arbitrary finite probability spaces
